profile.name: Mikołaj Szczęsny
profile.bio: I build things that make sound — real-time audio engines, signal-analysis tools, and VST plugins — mostly in C++ and Rust. Currently at Intel, based in Gdańsk, Poland.

featured.blurb: Modular C++17 toolkit for verifying audio integrity and computing quality metrics — SNR, MSE, spectral distance, THD, RT60 — on WAV files and live PortAudio streams. Catch2-tested, JSON reporting.
Parametric equalizer VST plugin built with JUCE, written as an engineering thesis project. Real-time biquad filtering with a custom GUI.
Lightweight C++ audio engine library designed as a foundation for real-time audio applications.
Measures the frequency-response curve of an audio path by playing a chirp through a chosen output and analyzing the captured input.
Minimal C++ example of real-time audio pass-through on a Raspberry Pi using ALSA — a starting point for embedded audio work.
LLM-powered dubstep pattern generator on top of Strudel: sample drums, sidechain ducking, halftime feel, live in-browser playback, and a VS Code Copilot skill.
A generalized regular-expression printing tool (grep-like) written in Rust as a language-learning project.
Python library and CLI for fetching coordinates, address details, and timezone data for any location. Published on PyPI.
Experiments integrating the Stockfish engine from C to get better at chess. Work in progress.
Simple Python spectrum analyzer for mono and stereo audio files.
